offer.title: Accept the public offer
offer.intro: Before you request a pilot or contact sales, confirm you accept the public offer for BidShard self-hosted software.
points: License runs on your VPS or dedicated server; vendor does not host your traffic by default.
Paid tiers differ by hosts, API keys, export limits, and feature flags in the JWT. Campaign and event volume are unlimited — scale on your hardware.
Monthly USDT fees are non-refundable after JWT delivery except vendor failure to deliver within 5 business days.
You are responsible for lawful use, VPS security, backups, and end-user privacy on your deployment.
Documented force majeure (host loss, provider shutdown, emergency relocation) may qualify for additional license activations at vendor discretion — contact support before rebinding hardware.

architecture.title: Hot path in milliseconds, cold path on your schedule
architecture.subtitle: Default appliance on your VPS: Nginx perimeter, tracker pool, Redis-backed filters, async processor. Campaign rules load from in-memory snapshots — admin writes never sit on the /track thread.
points: Ingest budget: filter chain and budget debit before async enqueue (sub-100ms target on /track)
At most one Redis script per accepted event — or zero when local quanta covers the shard
Processor worker settles Postgres spend and batches ClickHouse; HTTP 202 means accepted, not yet stored
Control API (:8188): RBAC, outbox, billing. IVT detector and fraud-scorer are cold-path sidecars — batch jobs on ClickHouse, never synchronous model inference on /track

highlights.title: Spend gate on ingest
highlights.body: Unified filter debits campaign budget and deduplicates clicks synchronously — rejected traffic does not spend.

highlights.title: Snapshots, not live Postgres on /track
highlights.body: Tracker reads atomic campaign registry and fraud boost maps; config reloads via Redis pub/sub after admin mutations.

highlights.title: Fail-closed budget pairing
highlights.body: Stream admission reserves capacity before Lua debit; if async enqueue fails, spend rolls back. current_spend never drifts above budget_limit.

highlights.title: Outbox after every admin write
highlights.body: Campaign edits, RBAC, and billing mutations land in Postgres first, then propagate through outbox workers — ingest never waits on SQL.

highlights.title: Postback hops you can audit
highlights.body: Conversion /track verifies inbound postback signatures; failed partner deliveries sit in DLQ with replay — disputes backed by event IDs, not screenshots.

highlights.title: LightGBM batch scorer, not LLM on ingest
highlights.body: fraud-scorer (Scale+) runs gradient-boosting (LightGBM) on scheduled ClickHouse batches. Scores land in Redis boost keys; the tracker hot path does snapshot lookup only — no chat API, no per-click external inference.

highlights.title: Optional depth when licensed
highlights.body: Broker WAL, eBPF edge drops, OpenRTB live auction — add when you need them, not required for a pilot.

contacts.title: Support and sales on Telegram
contacts.subtitle: Pilot license, paid tiers, HWID bind, and upgrades — message the support bot or manager directly. No ticket queue.
contacts.relocation_note: Lost a host or moving regions under force majeure? We understand media-buying ops — provider bans, seized DC, war-zone relocations. Message us with your deployment_id; we can grant extra license activations case by case.

margin_guard.title: Pause campaigns before profit turns red
margin_guard.body: Compares spend to payout in ClickHouse. When ROI drops below your threshold, campaigns pause automatically — not just a Telegram alert you read after the budget is gone.
margin_guard.footnote: Margin Guard watches ROI in ClickHouse while hot-path filters block spend on rejected traffic.

killers.title: Drop the cloaker bill
killers.body: Built-in funnel protection and safe-page checks — no $300–600/month third-party cloaker. Same protection on accepted traffic, more margin left after media spend.

killers.title: Bad traffic looks accepted — you do not pay
killers.body: Silent reject sends bots and reviewers a clean 202 while your budget stays intact. They see a normal funnel; you see every filtered hit in analytics.

killers.title: Where did 15 conversions go?
killers.body: Network says 100 leads, partner shows 85. Every postback hop is logged so you spot the gap — network, tracker, or affiliate — before the week closes in the red.

killers.title: ROI turned red? Campaign pauses, not just an alert
killers.body: Margin Guard compares spend to payout in ClickHouse every few minutes. Below your threshold the campaign pauses automatically — while hot-path filters still block junk spend.

killers.title: Stop feeding moderators
killers.body: Reviewers browse from clean residential IPs that pass blocklists. Flag mismatched device signals before they reach your money page — less ban risk, less wasted spend.

killers.title: Partner shave? Send proof, not screenshots
killers.body: Export clicks, postback receipts, and payout snapshots in one bundle — built for traffic refund disputes, not ticket ping-pong.

killers.title: Change servers without losing revenue days
killers.body: Slot migration moves ingest to new hardware under the same license — no week-long reinstall freeze while campaigns sit idle.

killers.title: Monetize inventory, not just buy traffic
killers.body: Live OpenRTB bid endpoint on your metal — take programmatic demand without bolting on a separate ad server stack.

killers.title: L4 junk hits your wire bill first
killers.body: eBPF XDP edge drops flood traffic before it reaches your tracker or bandwidth invoice — for installs under heavy bot waves or DDoS.

killers.title: Conversions networks can optimize on
killers.body: Meta, Google, and TikTok CAPI run on your VPS — real postback signal to the ad stack, not a Zapier relay or half-synced browser pixel.
